Proteomics Explorer B7_43 · FFPE primary colorectal tumour · mass spectrometry proteomics (Orbitrap Astral DIA)

Reference

Summary

Proteins measured in one primary colorectal tumour sample (B7_43, FFPE tissue) by mass spectrometry. No healthy tissue was usable as a reference.

The data shows

Which proteins are present

— proteins detected with confidence in the tumour sample. Detection does not show which cells in the sample made the protein, and a protein that was not detected may still be present at low levels.

The data does not show

Whether a protein is overexpressed

No healthy tissue was usable for a reference, so there is no direct comparator. Outside data on colorectal cancer in general (CPTAC tumour vs normal pairs, HPA cancer IHC) is shown beside each target instead. It describes other patients, not this tumour.

Antibody and ADC drug targets found in the tumour

— cell-surface proteins detected with confidence in the tumour have an antibody-based drug that is approved or in clinical trials (antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), and for CDH17, PTK7, GPA33 and CD276 also bispecific, radiolabelled antibody or CAR-T agents in trials). Details on page 2.

They are grouped by how many of two outside sources show the protein as raised or commonly stained in colorectal cancer in general. CPTAC: a study that measured tumour and nearby normal tissue from the same colorectal cancer patients, counted when the protein is consistently higher in tumour. HPA (Human Protein Atlas): tumour sections from up to 12 colorectal cancer patients stained for the protein, counted when at least half stained high or medium. These sources describe other patients, not this tumour.

Targets

What the columns mean

Antibody and ADC drugs
Drugs acting on the protein. The tag gives the most advanced stage reached in any disease (approved or trial phase). Trial numbers (NCT) are given where the drugs come from ClinicalTrials.gov.
Unique peptides
Number of protein fragments found in the tumour that belong only to this protein. More fragments means more certain detection (2 or more counts as confident).
CPTAC
"Up" when, in colorectal cancer patients studied by CPTAC, the protein was consistently higher in tumour than in the same patient's nearby normal tissue (higher in at least 75% of patients, statistically significant, and at least about 1.4-fold).
log2 T−N
Typical CPTAC difference between tumour and nearby normal tissue on a log2 scale. 0 means no difference, 1 means twice as much in tumour, −1 means half.
HPA
"50%+" when at least half of the colorectal tumours stained by the Human Protein Atlas showed high or medium staining.
H / M / L / ND
Number of HPA colorectal cancer patients whose tumours stained high, medium, low, or not detected.

Methods and limits

Why this tumour's own protein levels are not used to decide whether a protein is overexpressed, and the rules behind each column.

Control test of public normal references

ComparisonExpectedResult
Komor colorectal cancers vs Komor normal mucosa (same platform)Above 0.5—
27 PXD073413 Astral tumours vs Komor normal mucosaAbove 0.5—
27 PXD073413 Astral tumours vs HPA colonAbove 0.5—
This tumour vs Komor normal mucosaAbove 0.5—
This tumour vs HPA colonAbove 0.5—

For each comparison, every protein gets a score (its within-sample percentile in the query minus its median percentile in the reference). The result is the AUC for separating CPTAC tumour-up from tumour-down proteins (0.5 = no separation). Values for groups of query samples are medians. References: Komor PXD012254 (Q Exactive HF DIA, 19 normal and 30 cancer runs) and HPA v25.1 tissue proteome colon (3 samples).

Sample composition

Against the 27 PXD073413 colorectal tumours (Orbitrap Astral DIA), the number of tumours ranking below this tumour is — for EPCAM, — for MCM2, — for CEACAM5 (epithelium and proliferation), and —, —, — and — for DES, CNN1, MYH11 and COL1A2 (smooth muscle and stroma). Ranks are within-sample percentiles. The PXD073413 tumours are annotated "epithelial cell" in their sample sheet, with preparation not described. This tumour sample is an FFPE section cleared for analysis by the pathology centre.

Definitions

Confident detection
2 or more peptides unique to the protein group in the tumour sample, mapped to a single gene, not in the universal contaminant library. Others are flagged.
Evidence levels
Level 1: drug on the NCI list of FDA-approved drugs for colon and rectal cancer. Level 2: FDA-approved for another cancer (NCI A to Z list). Level 3: drug in a cancer clinical trial (Open Targets 26.09). Level 4: no drug in Open Targets, tractable. Mechanism of action must name the protein. CDH17 and PTK7 are Level 4 by these rules but appear on pages 1 and 2 because of the ClinicalTrials.gov check.
Cell surface
At least 2 of 4 sources: SURFY, CSPA, HPA plasma membrane, Open Targets high-confidence location.
Antibody or ADC
Open Targets drug type Antibody or Antibody drug conjugate, or a ClinicalTrials.gov trial whose title names the target or an agent with its stated target (CDH17, PTK7, GPA33, CD276, searched 21 Oct 2026). Trial agents include ADCs, bispecifics, radiolabelled antibodies and a CAR-T.
